finding.claim: Keys added with the ssh-agent CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM constraint are signed without invoking the Agent::confirm hook. try_sign replaces the confirmation with an always-true ready future, so a per-use confirmation prompt is never shown.
finding.source: Local client of the agent socket (any process that can connect to the agent) sends a SIGN request (msg 13) for a key that was loaded with the confirm constraint (msg 25 with constraint byte 2).
finding.sink: sign_with_hash_alg at keys/agent/server.rs:355 produces a signature with no user confirmation.

trace.note: Client sends add-identity-constrained (msg 25); add_key parses constraints.
CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM is pushed as Constraint::Confirm and stored in KeyStore (line 313).
try_sign looks up the key and reads its constraints.
needs_confirm is set when constraints contain Confirm.

BUG: when needs_confirm is true, the code builds Box::new(futures::future::ready((agent, true))) and never calls agent.confirm(key). The Agent::confirm trait method (server.rs:50-55) is the designed hook and is skipped.
The signature is produced without confirmation.

finding.guards_checked: is_locked check (server.rs:131-137, 158); generic confirm_request(Sign) gate (server.rs:57-59, default true, not the per-key confirm); key lookup. No code path calls Agent::confirm for the confirm constraint. Impact is only realised when an application overrides Agent::confirm to prompt; the library default returns true either way.

finding.claim: Receive-side channel flow control is not enforced: CHANNEL_DATA that exceeds the advertised window is still delivered to the handler, and the window is re-granted, so a peer can keep sending beyond the window without being disconnected.
finding.source: Remote SSH peer sending CHANNEL_DATA or CHANNEL_EXTENDED_DATA larger than the window it was granted.
finding.sink: handler.data / handler.extended_data (server/encrypted.rs:1048 and 1041) and the per-channel queue; unbounded growth happens only if the application buffers the data.

trace.note: CHANNEL_DATA/EXTENDED_DATA decoded; Bytes::decode limited by MAXIMUM_PACKET_LEN at the transport layer (cipher/mod.rs:313).
Window is decremented only if data.len() <= sender_window_size; otherwise the excess is silently ignored (comment: 'Ignore extra data').
When the window falls below target/2 a CHANNEL_WINDOW_ADJUST for target - window is sent, so an over-window peer gets more credit.

Data is still forwarded to the handler and to the channel (line 1043-1047). The channel is a bounded mpsc (channels/mod.rs:469), so the connection applies backpressure rather than growing memory, unless the application buffers the data itself.

finding.guards_checked: Per-packet MAXIMUM_PACKET_LEN (cipher/mod.rs:313); bounded channel buffer (channels/mod.rs:469) giving backpressure; the library does not disconnect or reject over-window data. Only the server path was traced in full; the client path shares session.rs adjust_window_size.

finding.claim: add_key writes an SSH_AGENT_SUCCESS byte before validating the constraint list. If a constraint is unknown or malformed, the key is not inserted, but the response carries SUCCESS followed by FAILURE, so the client is told the key was loaded when it was not and the reply has a malformed payload.
finding.source: Local agent client sending an add-identity-constrained request (msg 25) with an unknown constraint type or a truncated lifetime field.
finding.sink: The agent response written to the client (writebuf), which the client interprets as success.

trace.note: Caller: if add_key returns Ok(true) do nothing, else push FAILURE.
writebuf.push(SUCCESS) happens before the constraint loop.
Constraint loop: unknown type returns Ok(false) at line 310; a truncated lifetime returns Err via ? at line 290.
Key insertion is skipped on both early-return paths.
The caller then pushes FAILURE, so the payload is SUCCESS,FAILURE and the length prefix (235-236) covers both bytes.

finding.guards_checked: Frame length bound on the agent protocol (server.rs:107-110). Lock state check (131-137). The key is not inserted, so there is no key-material exposure; the defect is response integrity and a false success report.
